text:
Maya (Support): Hey team, escalated from Priya at AcmeCorp — streaming responses from their Dedicated instance over SSE are frequently dropping after ~20s and sometimes arriving as truncated partial events. Customer sees this only from internal corporate network. Repro steps below.

Priya (Customer): Repro: connect to our private endpoint behind corp proxy -> we get a few SSE events then connection closes. On reconnect client gets partial JSON and app crashes. Happens in browsers + server-side clients. Not happening from home network.

Maya (Support): Quick details: Dedicated instance in us-west-2 in their VPC, using on-prem ingress (F5) -> tunnels to our private NAT -> dedicated nodes. They mentioned MTU=9000 on their segments. Proxy is company-wide "secure-proxy" that does TLS termination and re-encrypts.

Arjun (Eng-runtime): Thanks — two likely suspects: 1) corporate proxy is buffering or cutting chunked responses (proxy buffering / timeouts), 2) MTU / fragmentation causing TCP-level issues for long-lived chunked transfer. SSE depends on streaming chunk semantics, proxies that buffer will hold the response and then flush or close unexpectedly.

Lena (Eng-infra): Can you get a sample client curl from them? Ask to run:

```
curl -v --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://private.redwood.example/sse?stream=chat" > /tmp/sse.out
```

and also run tcpdump on client side during repro: `sudo tcpdump -i any -s0 -w /tmp/sse.pcap host <dedicated-ip>`

Tom (Eng-sre): Also request the proxy config snippets for these keys: `proxy_buffering`, `proxy_request_buffering`, `proxy_read_timeout`/`keepalive_timeout`, any HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 conversion, and whether they are re-chunking or changing headers like `Connection` or `Transfer-Encoding`.

Priya (Customer): Running curl now, sending logs. When it drops I see: 
```
* read from 0x7fbbf400: Connection reset by peer
* Closing connection 0
```
and `sse.out` contains one partial JSON object like `{ "id": "evt_1234", "text": "This is a long stream that got cut` (truncated).

Maya (Support): They also attached F5 logs showing an active TCP FIN from proxy at the same time. Looks like proxy triggers timeout/idle detection.

Arjun (Eng-runtime): Two tests to isolate: 1) bypass the corporate proxy (direct VPN or mobile hotspot) — they already said it works from home, so that's a strong indicator. 2) Lower MTU on client path to 1500 or clamp MSS on the proxy/loadbalancer to avoid fragmentation. MTU=9000 often interacts poorly with intermediate devices that don't support jumbo frames — can create silent drop of large TCP segments.

Lena (Eng-infra): For MTU: ask them to set on the tunnel/loadbalancer `ip tunnel` or interface MTU to 1500 or apply `iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` on their egress. That usually prevents fragmentation-induced breaks.

Tom (Eng-sre): For proxies (nginx example), recommend disabling buffering and extending timeouts:

```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_request_buffering off;
proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
proxy_send_timeout 3600s;
keepalive_timeout 300s;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
```

Also ensure `proxy_http_version 1.1;` and `proxy_set_header Connection "";` so the socket is not closed by upstream header munging.

Priya (Customer): We changed `proxy_buffering` to off and increased timeouts. After testing we still see occasional truncation but less frequent. We then lowered MTU on the F5 to 1500 and the truncations stopped in ~90% of runs. Still seeing rare disconnects after ~10-15 minutes.

Arjun (Eng-runtime): Good data point — MTU/clamp seems to have been the main culprit for partial outputs. The remaining long-tail disconnects probably proxy idle or health check timeouts that close long lived connections. Ask them to scan logs for periodic L7 health-checks that may reset sockets.

Maya (Support): Customer asked if we can change the server side to use smaller chunks or send keepalive comment lines in SSE to prevent idle close. Is that something we can do from Redwood side?

Arjun (Eng-runtime): We can add periodic SSE keep-alive comments (`: keepalive\n\n`) from the runtime for streams that are idle for >15s. But that is a broad change — we should only enable as config for Dedicated/Private instances, since hosted customers may not want noisy heartbeats. Propose a per-deployment flag `streaming.idle_keepalive_interval` default off.

Lena (Eng-infra): Meanwhile advise customer to configure proxy to not treat idle streams as failed: set `proxy_read_timeout` high and avoid intrusive L7 inspection. Also suggest enabling HTTP/2 passthrough if their proxy supports it — though SSE over H2 has different semantics and some agents may not support event-stream over h2 well.

Priya (Customer): We'll try the keepalive header workaround on our client: send a `GET` then write a small `POST`? Not ideal. If you can add server-side keepalive comments for our Dedicated instance that would be great.

Tom (Eng-sre): We can do a targeted runtime config flip for their Dedicated cluster as a test. Need approval from security/compliance for on-prem/private changes — but since it's customer-specific and runtime-level, should be low risk. I'll open a change request.

infra-bot: Deployment change request created: CR-2025-113 - "enable streaming keepalive for acmecorp-dedicated" by Tom. CI/CD gating will run smoke tests.

Maya (Support): Action items: 1) Priya to confirm proxy buffer/timeouts and provide tcpdump/pcap for one failing run. 2) Priya to keep MTU at 1500/clamp MSS; 3) Tom to file CR and schedule a targeted toggle of `streaming.idle_keepalive_interval=15s` for their Dedicated cluster; 4) Arjun to prepare a minor runtime patch that emits SSE comment keepalives and honors config (feature flag).

Priya (Customer): Thanks — attaching pcap and proxy config. We'll run more tests tonight, will report results. Appreciate the quick turnaround 🙂

Maya (Support): Great, marking as escalated. Will follow up once CR lands and after Priya's pcap analysis.

Arjun (Eng-runtime): One more debugging tip to collect: `openssl s_client -connect <endpoint>:443 -quiet` then `GET /sse... HTTP/1.1` and watch binary behavior: sometimes TLS record fragmentation interacts with MTU/proxy. If they can reproduce with that it proves a TCP/TLS fragmentation issue.

Tom (Eng-sre): Noting: this thread differs from the usual "immediate disconnects" — it's partial event truncation plus reconnect causing duplicated partial payloads. Documenting for runbook: "SSE partial outputs often = MTU/fragmentation; SSE full disconnects often = proxy idle/health-check or header munging."

Maya (Support): Closing loop for now. Will reopen if new evidence arises.
